_strings.@@0c84aebc0231: Treaty conformity — CO conforms to federal treaty treatment — income exempt from federal tax under a treaty is also excluded from CO income (it flows through the federal starting point; do not add it back on the CO return). (This is about TREATY conformity only — a state can conform on treaties while DECOUPLING from the federal Code for deductions or credits; see any law-change lines below.) State note: Colorado's DR 0104 begins at "Federal Taxable Income" (line 1, taken directly from federal Form 1040/1040-SR/1040-SP). Federally treaty-exempt income is already excluded from federal taxable income, so it flows through to Colorado untaxed UNLESS Colorado has an explicit addback. The DR 0104's complete Additions to Federal Taxable Income (lines 2-7) are: state/local income or sales taxes from Schedule A, Qualified Business Income Deduction addback, Federal Deduction addback, nonqualified CollegeInvest distributions, nonqualified Colorado ABLE distributions, and Line 7 "Other Additions" (whose enumerated items in the 2023 booklet are: non-Colorado state/local bond interest, charitable conservation easement amounts also claimed for a CO credit, unauthorized alien labor expenses, partnership/fiduciary adjustments increasing federal taxable income, and restricted-membership club expenses). NONE of these is an addback of federally treaty-exempt or foreign-source income. Therefore treaty-exempt income is not re-taxed and Colorado conforms. (Confirmed against the official 2023 DR 0104 form and DR 0104 Booklet PDFs on tax.colorado.gov.)

Full-year residents enter the result directly; part-year residents apportion via DR 0104PN line 34. Children age 6 or older are not eligible.

Part-year residents apportion by the DR 0104PN line 34 percentage. (ITIN filers and certain filers under 25 use a separate form, DR 0104TN.)

Care must meet IRC Section 21 / IRS Pub 503 tests.

_strings.@@e1b4121af611: Property Tax/Rent/Heat Rebate (PTC Rebate) - low-income seniors and disabled — Full-year Colorado residents (lived in CO all of 2023) who paid property tax, rent, or heating bills in 2023, were not claimed as a dependent on another return, and met an age/disability test: age 65 or older on 12/31/2023; OR a surviving spouse (widow/widower) at least 58 years old on 12/31/2023; OR totally disabled for all of 2023 receiving full disability benefits. This is a standalone rebate application (not part of the income-tax return); 2023 applications were due by 12/31/2025.

citation.source: 2023 Colorado 104 Book (DR 0104 instructions) — "The income tax rate is currently 4.4%" (the document is the year-pinned 2023 filing guide); DR 0104 Line 1 = Federal Taxable Income from Form 1040/1040-SR/1040-NR/1040-SP; "Colorado income tax is based on your federal taxable income, which has already considered your deductions"; Line 10 = Colorado Taxable Income; booklet tax table row $30,700-$30,800 -> $1,353 (= 4.4% of the $30,750 midpoint).

state_tax.work_common_tail: 0. Tax line: DR 0104 Line 11 (Colorado Tax): full-year residents take the amount from the booklet tax table (built at 4.4%) for Line 10 Colorado Taxable Income (= Line 8 minus Line 9); part-year residents and nonresidents use DR 0104PN Line 36. This op computes the state's flat-rate tax line ONLY — county/city add-on taxes, state credits, and any amounts outside the rate schedule are NOT modeled. Pack notes: Colorado starts from federal TAXABLE income (DR 0104 Line 1) — the federal standard/itemized deduction is already embedded, so Colorado has no exemptions or separate standard deduction. The DR 0104 form itself does not print a multiplication — Line 11 says to use the tax table (or DR 0104PN Line 36). The booklet table is built at 4.4% but its $100-band rounding can differ from raw multiplication by a few dollars; the printed table row controls on the filed form.
